searchText: Would someone be kind enough to send me some test ether on the Rinkeby test network? The faucets aren't working for me ): Hello, just a silly question. Is it hard to contribute to eth with my skillset of 8years of RoR and JS ? The idea o being a part of "revolution" is very nice, but i doubt myself 🙂 Good news: 1559 has made gas fees more predictable. Bad news: also less affordable for some. https://twitter.com/takenstheorem/status/1427130936940851201 It seems to me that when the band is wider the fee is more predictable. A wider band means higher chance of the fee you picked being included. Its like the miners had a big shovel before now they only have a small one which is why the band is narrower but whatever i feel like its beating a dead horse 😄 EIP1559 is not going away It's definitely done what I think was supposed to be the goal - more predictable gas pricing. It's just unfortunate that it's raised the floor so as to totally eliminate low cost transactions. it has accelerated the reduction of ERC20 transactions it seems. But they are still in an uptrend. <#692078615269212180> is the appropriate place to talk about this, though keep in mind it should be research focused. This server isn't the right place to discuss sentiment, but rather a place to discuss research and data. Generally, I recommend against linking to Twitter. If you find something valuable to further research on Twitter, you can share it in this server as part of a larger discussion but we shouldn't be just linking Tweets along with some sentiment and nothing else. I would be curious to know the reason why the bottom peaks are not mantained while the top peaks are pure speculation but... The algorithm restricts how slow the base fee can drop, but users can always choose to send a transaction with a high "tip", so when the demand is really there, users/bots can push the cost of their transaction fees as high as they would like, but in times of low demand the rate the base fee falls is fixed by the algorithm Oh I thought those charts were base-fee, not including tips The tweet says: "Gas price estimated from 100,000 blocks, before/after #Ethereum London." if they include tips (which would be more accurate) to compare to gas price Ah yeah exactly but then it does not really matter much to me that have a transaction with tip of 1GWei and base fee < 20 waiting for a few days now 🙂 https://www.gwern.net/docs/www/eprint.iacr.org/d64c7bc76433490220640bfc59cfdb6c61d7e311.pdf Is there a way to use this to allow smart contracts to unlock files? I'm wondering why one can't simply fork the chain, change the difficulty/block time parameters, and speed up time that way. I must be missing something Valid q. I assume it must be checking validity of bitcoin transactions too then. Haven't read the paper, but I think you might be able to achieve it with something that is a function of total hashpower, rather than time. And you use hashpower as a proxy for time. Though, even that is still black magic. theyre using number of blocks which directly represents time difficulty adjustments ensure you're measuring time not hashpower You essentially are building a VDF where the delay piece of the function is "Bitcoin hashing". Now wondering if this can also check smart contract variables I'm still not convinced I can create my own bitcoin fork and fudge with the hashpower numbers, and blammo I'm done Nodes won't accept it. Whatever code nodes run will have to be put inside the witness encryption thing they're using I assume. I don't care if other nodes accept it, I want to know what's in the box Idk how witness encryption works (hence asking here), but they're converting the NP relation of what a valid blockchain is, into some encryption scheme. If my guess is right, the decryption requires X hashes. You could do X hashes yourself, but the Bitcoin mining network will do them faster. That still doesn't make any sense. How would it even verify if those hashes are correct <@!301186049323958275> do you think smart contracts can trigger file reveal then? Unless you somehow force Bitcoin miners to do the hashes you require to be done (they won't, because they have their own nonce problem to solve), I really don't see how this would work You don't need specific hashes though, you just need *any* hashes that solve this specific NP problem to generate a witness. And it's instantiated with genesis block or current block Black magic I say. So you can fill the chain with empty blocks to get that witness, but then you might be better off mining bitcoin Yes, in theory. Assuming you can use any arbitrary functional state transition as your delay function. So ethereum can be used to sell solutions to math problems? Or any file for that matter Instead of "after X has happened n times" you can say "after X returns y value". Again, that paper is making claims of black magic, but if my guess on how that magic works is correct, and the paper is legit, then yes. I am very much not a cryptographer, I just write cryptographic libraries against the recommendations of everyone. The lack of mentions of "forks" in that paper is alarming though If they are just counting hashes, then it isn't surprising because forks don't matter. Do you mean forks with same initial state and state transition function? idk if this is relevant Yeh, and then I can just increment the hash counter on my fork to some obscene number. So it can't be a naive counter. Using a VDF or something makes sense to me, if the time lock up period you require is equal to the work you put in before you published your challenge. And even then people need to actively work on _your_ problem, not some parallel problem like mining Bitcoin blocks. I imagine something like "the decryption key is 2 gazillion VDF cycles starting from 0x123456...". But who knows, maybe there is some moon math solution to all this 🤷‍♂️ Presumably, the black magic is actually verifying hashes/nonces. It isn't just looking at Bitcoin Core app output and trusting it. If you believe this is possible with a VDF, then just imagine a VDF where the difficulty function is a function that checks a 100 Bitcoin blocks for validity, or `n` Bitcoin blocks where `n` runs until difficulty of a checked block == some target value. It is the "you can do this with a VDF" that is black magic to me. If I accept that part, I can accept the "use Bitcoin hashing as the difficulty function" pretty easily. Those are paralell problem to me With a VDF you know the difficulty function up front, but you don't know the final solution to the difficulty function. With Bitcoin blocks, you know the function to produce a series of valid blocks up front, but you do not know the final solution to block production (what the `nth` block looks like). The piece I don't get is how you can encrypt something with a function you don't know the solution to. But I'm willing to trust that it is possible with crypto magic. I'm not 😛 https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/258.pdf might be useful Then first find the answer of how to encrypt something with a VDF. 😄 Presumably, that will shed a light on how you encrypt something with PoW blocks. Oh man I'm in need of a couple of solutions, where do I pay? Well, as I said, with a VDF it's easy if you do N work of time lock work yourself before publishing. But even then someone needs to actually do the exact same work you require, not the same VDF with some other input first see the paper and tell us if it's possible to build :p Idk if VDF if this right mental model for this The work being done is public record. I think the paper linked by ghosts_in_the_code is appropriate here (based on the abstract). And it is still black magic. <@!301186049323958275> > I want Ethereum to be around and useful in 10 years. I'm willing to sacrifice throughput today in order to ensure that is the case. > This is not a pump and dump for me. Do you have a position on technical debt? I know nothing about blockchains out there, but I could imagine that the need to be backward compatible can actually hurt a chain in rapidly changing times. So in principle I do not see it impossible that there may be a censorship resistant and decentralized network either already out there or in the works. Is there something like what Ethereum wants to be already out (as a form or paper in the arxiv I mean)? I don't follow other chains very closely anymore as I have been burned way too many times by centralized or semi-centralized blockchains masquerading as censorship resistant chains. It is certainly possible that a new chain exists that is censorship resistant and has already implemented a bunch of the features that Ethereum wants to implement (verkle tries, portal network, sharding, zk magic, etc.) and I just don't know about it. Trying to change the tires on the bus while it is driving down the street filled with school children is a very hard task, and someone launching a new chain doesn't have to do that. They can just start with the nice tires. yeah, that's the actual question, and since the network depends on having users, I wonder if there is a justified fear in technical debt or not... not that it matters when you are already in the bus and have a puncture. The thing that I see with Ethereum is that it has a roadmap. Lots of chains take one of the features from the roadmap, launch clean, and call themselves Ethereum killers. But they have no answers for all of the other pieces in the roadmap, and no ability to carry out the very tricky process of upgrading a live chain. As <@!301186049323958275> says, if a chain launches with _all_ of the proposed Ethereum features, or even a majority, I'd be interested, but to date nothing appears to be even attempting to do so. excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content:
The thing that I see with Ethereum is that it has a roadmap.  Lots of chains take one of the features from the roadmap, launch clean, and call themselves Ethereum killers.  But they have no answers for all of the other pieces in the roadmap, and no ability to carry out the very tricky process of upgrading a live chain.

As <@!301186049323958275> says, if a chain launches with _all_ of the proposed Ethereum features, or even a majority, I'd be interested, but to date nothing appears to be even attempting to do so.
